newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN boss appeals for cash for human rights monitors.
newsitem.headline: UN boss appeals for cash for human rights monitors.

text.p: The U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan appealed for donor funds on Thursday for the world body's cash-strapped human rights observers, whose major operations are in Rwanda, Burundi and the former Yugoslavia.
Annan, on his first visit to Geneva as the new U.N. chief, also promised to speed up restructuring of the Gevea-based human rights office.

"Quite a lot of the human rights work is done through voluntary contributions. We should encourage governments to be generous to give freely, willingly and generously for this important aim," he told a news conference.
He said the human rights office would also have to work harder and be more effective in Geneva. "Restructuring is going on and it will be pushed further," he said.

The body has more than 100 observers in Rwanda but only a handful in Burundi. Its field presence in the troubled African region has been seriously hampered by cash shortages, and critics say the headquarters has often been slow to react.
